name: Thomas House — shuttered brick residence

geometry.floor_status: DTM interpretation: west approach 55.2–55.4 m, north/south 55.4 m, east 55.9 m; the hedge conceals actual thresholds.

material_review.status: V4 original-texture palette retained; v5 repairs bounded pane-to-frame contacts and concealed caps. Native review pending.
material_review.actual_observed: Dark red brick with pale mortar; white shutters and entrance pediments; gray overlapping hip roof; one short masonry chimney. Hedge obscures the base.

proxy_assignments.wall_and_foundation: original bricks; actual brick observed, no stone plinth invented
proxy_assignments.roof: stone_brick stairs/slabs as medium-gray overlapping-unit proxy; actual product unknown
proxy_assignments.painted_trim: smooth_quartz stairs/slabs and quartz pillars, used for geometry and pale paint appearance
proxy_assignments.shutters: thin pale_oak_trapdoor panels; timber product and exact shutter substrate are unknown
proxy_assignments.door: Thin pale_oak_trapdoor skin in the opening, with an operable birch_door lower panel; original textures represent painted joinery.
proxy_assignments.hedge: oak_leaves: clipped foliage proxy, not identified species
proxy_assignments.glazing: white_stained_glass_pane for pale sash lines; does not identify real glass composition.

material_review.caution: Source RGB includes shadow/exposure/white balance. Colour alone is not material identity or intrinsic reflectance. Original Minecraft textures only.

roof_evidence.rule: All 14 source faces are hash/polygon/plane checked. Keep exact footprint and major/flat roof surface controls; explicit high/low masks extend named adjacent planes. Fragment 0 identity is unresolved. One photographed bow-top dormer is authored, never a survey claim. Flat-end roof top heights remain while exposed backing is brick below one slab of coping.

dormer.status: One observed bow-top dormer; v2 narrows the pale border and gives its broader sash a compact quarter-metre brow, after native v1 review.

chimney.status: one short red chimney visible above roof; exact position interpreted

window_rows.evidence: far-left, near-centre and far-right groups visible; pole/pine-screened count and exact spacing interpreted
lower openings partly hedge/pole concealed; metric interpretation
broader near-centre lower sash is partly visible; screened counterpart interpreted

evidence.supports: West long two-storey red-brick elevation, white shutters/frames, separate triangular door pediments at both ends, gray hip roof, one curved dormer, short chimney and hedge hiding the base.
Campus identity and measured residence location.

uncertainties: Only west facade is independently photographed. Pine, pole and hedge conceal several sash groups; exact west counts/spacing are partly interpreted.
North, east and south windows are individual typological proposals, not observed elevations. Only one front curved dormer is authored; unseen dormers are not invented.
The hedge hides threshold and lower wall. The 55.75 m entry/floor, steps and hedge line/height are terrain/photo interpretations. No gray-stone plinth is evidenced.
Exact roof product, painted shutter substrate, chimney position and foliage species are unresolved. Minecraft block names identify proxies only.
Fragment 0 might be an unobserved architectural detail or reconstruction error; this study extends accepted west roof face 7 over its small footprint and records that choice.
Curved dormer and pediment profiles, shutter panels and glass are quantised at 2 blocks/metre. Native v4 review is required.
native_revision_notes: V1 native showed a tall slit dormer, projecting plank door boxes, shelf-like pediments and excessive gray roof-edge backing. V2 changes only these details, shutter attachment and pale sash texture.
West source wall U is nearly continuous, not deeply stepped; retain its 9.02136-degree surveyed orientation and ordinary half-metre raster steps.
All shutters now select actual brick attachment columns; no shutter cell is intentionally placed over glazing.

V2 all-field top slabs were rejected for a daylight layer. V3 keeps the solid inner roof; perimeter top slabs require solid inward backing, with solid brick closures at raster corners. Window aperture edge cells are fully glazed.
The user-requested diagonal joint audit found six open north-window pane corners in v3. V4 adds one inward pane return per joint, bounded to each original window reveal, without overwriting masonry.

V5 restores the exact hash-bound v4 archive, adds 33 inward pane-to-jamb returns with full concealed caps, caps four old north returns, and completes one wall-plane hood/sill intersection. It preserves the authored roof and original glazing.

accepted_baseline.rule: Exact native-reviewed v4 state archive; only the enumerated inward frame contacts below may change.
